description: Focused landmark-direction physical-dynamics run with balanced landmarks, crossing directions, and verb types.
notes: Generate 60 documents from 30 balanced landmark-direction cells.
The grid is 5 landmarks x 2 crossing directions x 3 verb types: explicit, direction_biased, and direction_neutral.
Each cell records entity, initial relation to landmark, later relation to landmark, and mechanism.
The family is designed to reduce shortcuts such as one landmark always implying one direction.

physical_dynamics_profile.definition: Can a model connect evidence about directional physical change, motion, and state/process change over time to the right event/process concept?
physical_dynamics_profile.centrality_rule: The cause, physical process, and outcome must be central; the document should not be solvable from object identity, landmark identity, or verb identity alone.
generation_guidance: Make the before/after landmark relation visible: the entity starts on one side of the landmark and later is on the other side.
Keep the mechanism visible, such as helium lift, buoyancy, motor lift, pulley lift, wind, gravity, release, lowering, or sinking.
Use the configured event_verb naturally as the assigned surface form for the event.
For direction-neutral verbs such as passed, crossed, and went by, make the initial and later relations carry the direction.
Balance landmarks in both directions; avoid making one landmark always mean upward or downward motion.

path_shape_policy.guidance: For landmark-direction examples, path_shape marks the relation crossing, such as upward_past_landmark or downward_past_landmark.

document_types.description: A compact physical event that names the cause and result.
A comparison between the expected process and a contrast process.
A concrete observation record of cause, motion, and outcome.

families.label: landmark-based directional change
families.schema: A physical entity changes relation to a landmark over time; the direction is determined by initial relation, later relation, and mechanism, not by the landmark alone.

discourse_styles.description: A small everyday moment from the perspective of a child noticing what changed.
guidance: Write like a child or nearby adult noticed one concrete landmark-crossing event.
Use the landmark relation naturally, not as a formal label.
Make the before relation, later relation, and mechanism visible.

discourse_styles.description: A plain explanation of one directional crossing dynamic, with the scenario as the central example.
guidance: Start with the physical idea, then use the scenario as the central example.
Name the mechanism and the before/after landmark relation.
Avoid turning the item into a quiz or answer key.

discourse_styles.description: A practical note about why the same landmark could be crossed in the other direction under a different setup.
guidance: Mention the contrast only to clarify the direction that did not happen.
Keep the actual before/after relation more central than the contrast.
Avoid implying that the landmark alone determines the direction.

discourse_styles.description: A brief field-note-style record of one visible landmark crossing.
guidance: Use compact note style, but avoid labels like Cause, Process, and Outcome.
Let the event order carry the mechanism, direction, and relation change.
Include one direct event sentence with the entity as subject.
